Counsel for Applicant :- Lalji Yadav,Balram Yadav Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.
1.Heard Sri Lalji Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Vishwa Nath Nishad, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State.

2. As per learned counsel for the applicant, the present applicant (Nitin Kumar Pal) is languishing in jail since 02.03.2024 in Case Crime No.43 of 2024, under Sections 376, 504 & 506 I.P.C., Police Station-Manikpur, District-Pratapgarh.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the present applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case as he has not committed any offence as alleged in the prosecution Nitin Kumar Pal vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

4.

The attention of this Court has been drawn towards the impugned First Information Report (in short F.I.R.) which has been lodged on 27.02.2024 for the alleged incident dated 12.02.2024 and the aforesaid delay in lodging the impugned F.I.R. has not been explained by the informant.
The informant has given information to the police on 19.02.2024 regarding the incident of rape.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that if the aforesaid prosecution story is considered on its face value, even then, there is no explanation of delay of seven days.

He has further submitted that the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. clearly indicates that someone has told to her husband about the incident then her husband reached at the place of incident whereas in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and in the F.I.R., it has been indicated that she raised alarm, on that, her husband reached at the place of incident.

Since there is an inordinate delay in lodging F.I.R., therefore, medical examination of the prosecutrix could not be conducted forthwith and such medical examination was conducted after about 16 days.

He has further submitted that the present applicant is a student aged about 22 years and the victim/
prosecutrix is a married lady aged about 27 years.

In her statement and in the F.I.R. she has not alleged that the alleged incident has been committed by the present applicant on the basis of any threat to life etc. and if no threat to life was given by the present applicant, the offence of rape by a single person with a young lady may not be committed, therefore, the prosecution story is misconceived.
The applicant is having no previous criminal history of any kind whatsoever.
The charge-sheet has been filed in this case.

Learned counsel for the applicant has undertaken on behalf of the present applicant that the applicant shall not misuse the liberty of bail, if so granted by this Court and shall abide by all terms and conditions of the bail order and shall cooperate with the trial proceedings.

6. On the other hand, learned Additional Government Advocate has, however, opposed the prayer for bail of the present applicant by submitting that since the role of the present applicant was found in the commission of crime, therefore, he is not entitled for grant of bail, but he could not dispute the aforesaid contention of learned counsel for the applicant.

7. Considering the fact that the prosecution story is not consistent as it varies from the F.I.R. to the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and Section 164 Cr.P.C., the charge-sheet has been filed and perusing the material available on record, arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and the undertaking that the applicant shall not misuse the liberty of bail, if so granted by this Court and shall abide by all terms and conditions of the bail order and shall cooperate with the trial proceedings properly, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, I find it appropriate that the present applicant may be enlarged on bail.

8. Let the applicant (Nitin Kumar Pal) be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-

(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fail to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then,
the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
The present applicant shall not leave the country without prior permission of the Court.

[Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.] Order Date :- 15.5.2024 Suresh/
